purpose: Distinguish a respondent's self-concept or belief in momentary internal guidance from any reliable physiological or birth-derived safety signal. Positive self-identification need not establish objective truth; missing/negative self-label alone is not evidence against predicted signal.
version: NEW EXPLORATORY HYPOTHESIS NOT V1 HISTORICAL SCORE RULE

constructs.meaning: A participant believes a brief intuitive cue exists and may be worth following; respondent-reported psychological belief, not empirical accuracy of a cue
constructs.measured_as: behaviorally neutral survey asked before any system/chart disclosure and checked on repetitions

constructs.meaning: A participant consciously noticed an event they interpreted as brief intuition; later recall and missed signals are unknown
constructs.measured_as: predefined prospectively recorded events with clear initial time and signal

constructs.meaning: A momentary cue reliably differentiates harmful from safe outcomes
constructs.measured_as: predefined time-bounded verifiable outcome, false positives/negatives and matched control

admission_logic.if: positive belief and chart not disclosed, no control rates
positive belief after participant learned HD Splenic label
no explicit belief or cue recollection
positive or negative belief with independently measured birth-group endorsement rates
subjective belief reported as factually infallible safety cue

research_output: Optional qualitative compatibility annotation with provenance and evidence-status, never primary model weight until prospective comparative human data.
